# easyai

> easyai teaches non-technical people how to use AI tools. Instead of watching videos,
> the learner pastes a short lesson into the tool itself and it becomes a tutor that
> walks them through a real task, one step at a time, waiting for an answer at each step.

## What makes it different

Most AI courses are videos of someone else using AI. easyai lessons run **inside** the
tool being learned. A lesson is a few lines of plain text the learner pastes into ChatGPT,
Claude Code, Copilot or Perplexity. The tool then gives one step, stops, and asks what
happened before continuing. "It didn't work" is always an accepted answer.

## Who it is for

People who do not consider themselves technical: teachers, nurses, shop owners,
freelancers, office workers, retirees, nonprofit staff. Not for software developers.

## Courses

- **ChatGPT** (available) — six lessons: ask your first question, ask better questions,
  turn a mess into a plan, make a coloring page, check if a message is a scam,
  know what not to share.
- **Claude Code** (available) — set it up without a terminal, then build something real.
- **Microsoft Copilot** (queued) — Copilot inside Word, Excel and Outlook.
- **Perplexity** (queued) — answers you can check, with sources.

## Facts

- Every lesson takes about ten minutes.
- Everything works on the free plans of each tool.
- No coding is required at any point.
- The starter kit is free.
- Independent: not affiliated with, endorsed by, or sponsored by OpenAI, Anthropic,
  Google or Microsoft.

## Pages

- [Home](https://easyaifornontechies.com/): the starter kit, how lessons work, the course list, FAQ.
- [The free ChatGPT course](https://easyaifornontechies.com/chatgpt-lessons/): all six lessons
  described; lesson one in full on the page.
- [How to write ChatGPT prompts](https://easyaifornontechies.com/how-to-write-chatgpt-prompts/):
  lesson two. The four additions that turn a vague request into a good answer: who it is for,
  what good looks like, what to avoid, something to look at.
- [Use ChatGPT to make a plan](https://easyaifornontechies.com/use-chatgpt-to-make-a-plan/):
  lesson three. Type a dreaded task messily and get it back organised by day; ask what is wrong
  with the plan rather than whether it is good.
- [How to install Claude Code](https://easyaifornontechies.com/how-to-install-claude-code/):
  the desktop-app route, about five minutes, no terminal required.
- [ChatGPT for nonprofits](https://easyaifornontechies.com/chatgpt-for-nonprofits/):
  donor thank-yous, grant drafts, and what must never be pasted in.
- [ChatGPT for lawyers](https://easyaifornontechies.com/chatgpt-for-lawyers/):
  why it invents case citations, and the drafting work it genuinely does well.
- [ChatGPT for accountants](https://easyaifornontechies.com/chatgpt-for-accountants/):
  it cannot do arithmetic reliably; what it can do is the rest of the job.
- [ChatGPT for teachers](https://easyaifornontechies.com/chatgpt-for-teachers/):
  differentiation in minutes, and why an AI detector score is not evidence.
